subproblem.title: Weighted and unweighted approximate tangent spaces coincide a.e. (Lemma B; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1))
subproblem.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[k] on ℝ^N, let E ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable with H(E ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, and let θ : ℝ^N → ℝ satisfy θ > 0 on E and be H-integrable on E ∩ K for every compact K. Then for H-a.e. x ∈ E (H⌞E-a.e.) and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^N: Q is the approximate tangent space of E at x with respect to θ (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q, Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7: finrank Q = k and ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH as r → 0+ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N)) if and only if Q is the unweighted approximate tangent space of E at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q, Def. 1.4).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (E : Set (Eucl N)) (θ : Eucl N → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) (E ∩ K) < ∞) → (∀ x ∈ E, 0 < θ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ (E ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)).restrict E), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl N), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q ↔ Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma B (weights; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1)) of Step 5 of the parent proof, with its sketch completed. It uses the siblings lusin_pieces (lpf_wtc_lusin_compact_pieces, comparator-accepted), zero_density (imc_ae_zero_density_off_set) and blowup_cov (lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image, comparator-accepted).

Notation. H := μHE[k]; η_{x,r} := blowUpMap x r, η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x), so x + r·η_{x,r}(z) = z; B̄_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and r > 0: I_u(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f dH and I_w(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y). HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q: finrank Q = k and I_u(r) → ∫_Q f dH (r → 0+) for every f; HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q: finrank Q = k and I_w(r) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH for every f.

1. (Change of variables.) By blowup_cov (Q := N, n := k, y := x, S := E), applied to g := f and to g := (y ↦ f(y)θ(x + ry)), for every r > 0:
 I_u(r) = r^{−k}∫_E f(η_{x,r}(z)) dH(z) and I_w(r) = r^{−k}∫_E f(η_{x,r}(z)) θ(z) dH(z).

2. (Lusin pieces.) The sibling lusin_pieces (Q := N, n := k, V := univ, M := E; its hypotheses are ours, every compact K lies in univ) gives compact sets C_i ⊆ E (i ∈ ℕ) such that θ|C_i is continuous, H(C_i) < ∞, and H(E ∖ ⋃_i C_i) = 0.

3. (Density zero off the pieces.) Fix i and put S_i := E ∖ C_i, which is H-null-measurable. For compact K, ∫⁻_{S_i∩K} 1 dH ≤ H(E ∩ K) < ∞ and ∫⁻_{S_i∩K} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dH ≤ ∫⁻_{E∩K} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dH < ∞. Applying zero_density twice (Q := N, n := k, S := S_i, with g := 1 and with g := ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ), for H-a.e. y ∉ S_i — in particular for H-a.e. y ∈ C_i —:
 (a) H(S_i ∩ B̄_ρ(y))/ρ^k → 0 and (b) (∫_{S_i ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} θ dH)/ρ^k → 0 as ρ → 0+.
 Let G_i be the set of y ∈ C_i at which (a) and (b) hold, and G := ⋃_i G_i. Then E ∖ G ⊆ (E ∖ ⋃_i C_i) ∪ ⋃_i (C_i ∖ G_i) is H-null, so H⌞E-a.e. x lies in G. The set G depends neither on Q nor on f.

4. (Error terms at a good point.) Fix x ∈ G, choose i with x ∈ G_i and write C := C_i, S := S_i. Then x ∈ E, so θ(x) > 0. Since θ|C is continuous at x, for every ε′ > 0 there is s(ε′) > 0 with |θ(z) − θ(x)| ≤ ε′ for all z ∈ C ∩ B̄_{s(ε′)}(x); in particular θ ≥ θ(x)/2 on C ∩ B̄_{s₁}(x), where s₁ := s(θ(x)/2).
 Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), R > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0), and ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|; put D(r) := r^{−k}H(C ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) for r > 0. For r > 0, z ↦ f(η_{x,r}(z)) is bounded by ‖f‖_∞ and vanishes off B̄_{Rr}(x); as H(E ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) < ∞ and θ is integrable on E ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x), all integrals below are finite, and E is the disjoint union of the null-measurable sets C and S. Splitting the integrals of Step 1 accordingly:
 (a′) |r^{−k}∫_S f(η(z))θ(z) dH| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ R^k (∫_{S∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} θ dH)/(Rr)^k → 0 (θ > 0 on S; Step 3(b));
 (b′) |r^{−k}∫_S f(η(z)) dH| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ R^k H(S ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x))/(Rr)^k → 0 (Step 3(a));
 (c′) for Rr ≤ s(ε′): |r^{−k}∫_C f(η(z))(θ(z) − θ(x)) dH| ≤ ε′‖f‖_∞ D(r).
 Since I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r) = r^{−k}∫_C f(η)(θ − θ(x)) dH + r^{−k}∫_S f(η)θ dH − θ(x)r^{−k}∫_S f(η) dH, we get |I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r)| ≤ o(1) + ε′‖f‖_∞ D(r) for Rr ≤ s(ε′).

5. (D is bounded under either hypothesis.) Let g_R(y) := max{0, min{1, R + 1 − ‖y‖}}; g_R ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), 0 ≤ g_R ≤ 1, g_R = 1 on B̄_R(0), so g_R(η_{x,r}(z)) = 1 for z ∈ B̄_{Rr}(x).
 - If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q: by Step 1 (with g_R in place of f), D(r) ≤ r^{−k}∫_E g_R(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} g_R dH → ∫_Q g_R dH, so D(r) ≤ ∫_Q g_R dH + 1 for all small r > 0.
 - If HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q: for Rr ≤ s₁, as g_R ≥ 0 and θ > 0 on E, Step 1 gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} g_R(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) = r^{−k}∫_E g_R(η(z))θ(z) dH(z) ≥ r^{−k}∫_{C∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} θ dH ≥ (θ(x)/2)·D(r); the left side tends to θ(x)∫_Q g_R dH, so D(r) ≤ 2(θ(x)∫_Q g_R dH + 1)/θ(x) for all small r > 0.
 In both cases there are D₀ < ∞ and r₀ > 0 with D(r) ≤ D₀ for 0 < r < r₀.

6. (Comparison.) Assume either hypothesis and let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), ε″ > 0. Choose ε′ > 0 with ε′‖f‖_∞ D₀ < ε″; by Steps 4 and 5, |I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r)| < 2ε″ for all sufficiently small r > 0. Hence I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r) → 0 as r → 0+, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N).

7. (Conclusion.) Let x ∈ G and Q a subspace. (⇐) If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q, then for every f, I_u(r) → ∫_Q f dH and by Step 6 I_w(r) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH; with finrank Q = k this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q. (⇒) If HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q, then by Step 6 θ(x)I_u(r) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH for every f, and θ(x) > 0 gives I_u(r) → ∫_Q f dH; with finrank Q = k this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q. Since H⌞E-a.e. x lies in G (Step 3), the equivalence holds H⌞E-a.e., for all Q simultaneously. ∎
proof_key_steps: Change of variables (blowup_cov): I_u(r) = r^{−k}∫_E f∘η, I_w(r) = r^{−k}∫_E (f∘η)θ.
Lusin pieces C_i ⊆ E with θ|C_i continuous and H(E∖⋃C_i) = 0; zero_density gives density 0 of H⌞(E∖C_i) and θH⌞(E∖C_i) at a.e. point of C_i.
At such x: I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r) = o(1) + O(ε′·r^{−k}H(C_i ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x))) by continuity of θ|C_i.
r^{−k}H(C_i ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) stays bounded under either hypothesis (test with g_R; θ ≥ θ(x)/2 near x on C_i).
Hence I_w − θ(x)I_u → 0, and θ(x) > 0 makes the weighted and unweighted conditions equivalent.

audit.reason: The proof establishes both directions of the exact contract. Lusin pieces and two zero-density applications control the complement; continuity controls weight oscillation. The required density bound is proved under either tangent hypothesis, and positivity justifies division by θ(x).
